title: Training Note — The Medical Baseline Allowance on One Service Agreement at a Time (Medical and Life-Support Protections)
content:
**The rule.** Under Medical and Life-Support Protections the medical baseline allowance follows the patient's full-time residence, so a customer receives an allowance on only one service agreement at a time: an application for an allowance kind is not accepted while the customer's count of allowance agreements is already one or more. Protections without an allowance (the Medical Emergency Certificate) are judged per agreement.

## Terms used in the rule

- **Allowance kind**: a protection whose medical baseline allowance is above zero — the Standard Medical Baseline Allowance, the Heating and Cooling Medical Baseline Allowance, the Combined Medical Baseline Allowance, the Life-Support Registration and the Critical Care Life-Support Registration. The Medical Emergency Certificate carries no allowance.
- **Count of allowance agreements**: the number of the customer's service agreements that, on the handling date, hold a medical certification in pending certification or active status of an allowance kind. Every agreement in the customer's portfolio is counted, whatever its address.

## Points of judgement

| Application | Customer's count of allowance agreements on the handling date | Outcome under this rule |
|---|---|---|
| for an allowance kind | 0 | not stopped by this rule |
| for an allowance kind | 1 or more | not accepted |
| for the Medical Emergency Certificate | any | not judged by this count; judged per agreement |

A certification that is denied, expired or withdrawn is not in pending certification or active status and so does not add to the count.

## Basis questions answered

**Does a pending application count, or only an active one?** Both count. An agreement holding an allowance-kind certification in pending certification status adds one to the count just as an active one does.

**Does the count look only at the address in the application?** No. It looks across all of the customer's service agreements on the handling date.

**Does a Medical Emergency Certificate held on one agreement affect an allowance application on another?** No. The Medical Emergency Certificate is not an allowance kind and is not counted.

### Hypothetical cases

1. A customer holds an active Heating and Cooling Medical Baseline Allowance at one address and applies for a Standard Medical Baseline Allowance at a second address. The count is 1, so the application is not accepted.
2. A customer's only allowance-kind certification, a Life-Support Registration, is expired, and the customer applies for a Combined Medical Baseline Allowance on another agreement. The expired certification is not counted; the count is 0 and this rule does not stop the application.
3. A customer holds an active Critical Care Life-Support Registration at one address and applies for a Medical Emergency Certificate at another. The application is not for an allowance kind, so this count is not applied to it.
